subject: The box pool's collision safeguards are console discipline, not server enforcement
description: Mallory PROVED 2026-09-20: a HAND-PLACED assignment (no fromPool, the way boxes were wired before the pool existed) is structurally invisible to every safeguard in the pool feature, because it never touches box_pool. Her reproduction: H1 (ended) holds a hand-placed assignment for url X; H2 legitimately wires the pool box carrying url X through every check - claim check, duplicate-URL check, transaction, all green - and both tournaments then serve the identical url AND password. ctfGetBoxCredential (functions/index.js:8191) reads the assignment doc and returns url/username/password with NO box_pool lookup at all, so it would serve that document verbatim. She confirmed the Firestore state by direct read but deliberately did NOT invoke the live callable, because the functions emulator can fire real webhooks from functions/.env under the standing rule from a prior incident, so the serving half is cited from source rather than executed. REMEDY, which is a FUNCTIONS change and widens the deploy surface: ctfGetBoxCredential should refuse to serve a credential whose provenance does not match box_pool's current claim, or refuse any credential without verifiable provenance. Every fix so far (claim, release status gate, revocation, transactions) is console discipline over one field that the hand-placed workflow bypasses by construction and always will. SECOND ITEM, same root cause of manual remedies: releaseOrphanedClaims has no cron, no scheduled function, no automation of any kind - grep finds only the console button and two test suites - so the remedy for a stranded claim equals the operator's memory.
